title: Mule-Head Attachment for a Couch
description: This bronze attachment in the shape of a mule’s head was once part of a fulcrum (armrest) for a banqueting couch. The mule’s mane flies upward, its mouth open and its ears pushed back against its head. The mule wears an ivy garland and a saddlecloth made from panther skin, two elements associated with the wine god Dionysos.
did_you_know: The pattern on the panther skin, called a meander, was also extremely popular on Greek pottery.
creditline: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
